Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 3132dacead062fa63c070fc7f404f8cf93df43a0
what association are we using here?
Is that defined in PDI ? Can you add that to the commit msg ?

https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/e4a64ba768a675937bcb41c5e74098c26de1d5e2/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item/README.md?plain=1#L27 

I would think it would be connected_to / connecting association more than containing..?
It's being put up. I will link it here once it is up.

PDI is not needed. This patch uses one existing PDI now `xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.PCIeSwitch`. https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item/PCIeSwitch.interface.yaml
Let's mark WIP until this is done. :)
This is 700 lines of new code.. Going to need more in the commit msg about why you need this
Updated the commit message for it.
I don't think we have done Conditions yet, can we leave this out or at least a separate commit.. I havne't seen a design for how it would work
No. Route handler for this URI is in file `redfish-core/lib/switch_port.hpp`.

Fabric Adapter is pretty broad but I don't know anything about your device. 
```
A fabric adapter represents the physical fabric adapter capable of connecting to an interconnect fabric. Examples include, but are not limited to, Ethernet, NVMe over Fabrics, Gen-Z, and SAS fabric adapters.
```

This would be simplier if you didn't have to implement the Switch / Fabric
Added the information about the device in the commit message.
Can you talk more about this device?
Missing some includes. include array, string_view, string, memory, boost error_code, d-bus
Can we remove HealthRollup ? I don't think we have a design for it
Is this association documented in PDI ?
No this is yet to be done.
This is not used anymore as we have static Fabric resource.
Huh ? I still see it in the commit msg.. What if you had multiple fabrics? How would you tie the switches to the correct Fabric?
If we plan to add support for multiple fabrics in future we can define an inventory decorator PDI for fabrics and associate switches to the appropriate fabric.

Can we do that now? (I would really prefer this) Or at least call out that this assumes 1 Fabrics and all switches are assumed under that fabric in the commit msg and probably as a code comment as well.

It is already called out in the commit message that this patch assumes single Fabric resource. - https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/84284/8//COMMIT_MSG#26

I have added that as a code comment as well.
Why wouldn't these 2 be together? Oh well.
Why don't they strictly qualify as a Fabric Adapter ?
@ed@tanous.net mentioned that Nvidia ConnectX should not be considered a FabricAdapter. @ed@tanous.net, can you please provide your input?

Maybe the commit message needs to be reworded, but why would we consider modeling a fabric switch (PCIe switch in this case) as a fabric adapter? Where is the expectation to model this as a fabric adapter (the commit message seems to suggest such an expectation) coming from @haghera@nvidia.com?

bmcweb already supports Fabric Adapter URI, so Gunnar questioned why it can't be used for ConnectX. And so, I included a clarification regarding this in the commit message. https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/84284/comment/4c58deb0_f809219c/

Can we get this documented in PDI? 
I don't see this documented. 
https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aopenbmc%2Fphosphor-dbus-interfaces+++++connecting&type=code

Inventory associations are collectively documented in https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item.interface.yaml (as opposed to replicating in all interfaces). The associations used here are documented as well.

The only place I see connecting is for Cables there 
https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item.interface.yaml#L122

I see a few more at https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/669f3182ab0001f6812875b884ecfbfbd1c8ae2c/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item/README.md?plain=1#L28
but nothing around Switch

Either make it more generic (so they are collectively documented) or push a new Inventory.Item type for connecting
I struggle with this being better than just supporting multiple fabrics, pulling the id from D-Bus, and having an association between fabric and switch
@deepak.kodihalli.83@gmail.com, can you please provide your input?
I wouldn't say this is better, but it is sufficient. Multi-fabric is not solved yet and wasn't required in this/related patches. Ed had this suggestion as well.
Why can't this be an enum ?
Unlike PortType, the generated enums do not include an enum for PortProtocol.
I think it is better to name as `switchInterfaces` so that additional interface may be added in the future
Those are not added as they are not needed as of yet, will be added in next set of patches if required at that time.
This is uint64 now in the PDI.
I have went through the checklist and had done the rework accordingly. Please let me know if I had missed anything.
?  This isn't maybe unused, it's unused.  Just don't include it?
This function is passed as a callback to the function getFabricSwitchPath, which is used at multiple places to get Switch Object Path.

Please don't call callbacks in a loop.  Push these to an array, and call the callback with the array (or an error).

If this list is empty, the callback won't be called.  If it contains multiple, it will be called multiple times.  Both are incorrect

Missing asserts for Fabrics.  This shouldn't just be incremented without adding the new properties.

Please fix in the next patch.
